question: which of the 18 exists()-filtered input-group call sites CAN silently shrink and which cannot, and for the 6 varying groups whether each variation is legitimate scope or a silent shrink

rule.committed_at: d31dd3d, before any call site was read

classes.REFUSES: the site raises, exits or otherwise returns an error on a short set rather than filtering it away. DECIDABLE TEST, from the code alone: the function enclosing the `files_entry` call contains a `raise` or a `SystemExit`/`sys.exit` whose reachability depends on a test over the globbed collection -- its length, its emptiness, a set difference against the expected members, or a per-member `.exists()` assertion. A refusal makes the remaining questions moot, because a short set never reaches the manifest
classes.CANNOT_SHRINK: every file the UNFILTERED glob can match is tracked in git, so a missing file is a tracked-file absence that the repository's existing guards already catch, and the `.exists()` filter can only ever drop a file whose absence is already loud. DECIDABLE TEST: the glob's directory prefix resolves to a literal path from the code, the unfiltered pattern matches at least one file on disk, and `git ls-files` reports EVERY matched file as tracked. THIS MUST BE PROVEN AND NOT ASSUMED: a directory under `data/knowledge`, `data/cache` or `data/reference` is git-ignored and is never this class, however tracked-looking its name
classes.SCOPE_IS_DECLARED_ELSEWHERE: the result's own artefact states the expected scope from a source INDEPENDENT of the glob -- an expected count, a chromosome list or a sample list -- so a shrink is detectable from the artefact by comparing the two. DECIDABLE TEST: the same manifest-writing function records a second entry (a parameter, a value entry or another input) whose value derives from the same constant or argument that feeds the glob and NOT from the filtered list, so that a short glob leaves the artefact internally inconsistent. A scope derived from the filtered list itself does NOT qualify, because it shrinks with it
classes.CAN_SHRINK_SILENTLY: the site filters on `.exists()` and records whatever is present, with no refusal, no tracked directory and no independent record of the expected scope. DECIDABLE TEST: the glob's directory resolves, at least one matched file is NOT tracked in git, and neither the REFUSES nor the SCOPE_IS_DECLARED_ELSEWHERE test is met. These are the live sites of the defect
classes.UNDECIDABLE_FROM_THE_CODE: the facts the four tests above need cannot be resolved statically -- the glob's directory or its expected member set is built from a runtime argument, a configuration value, or a function of another module whose return is data-dependent -- so no class can be decided without running the program or opening a store. DECLARED IN ADVANCE AS A LEGITIMATE OUTCOME: a site in this class is reported as undecidable with the fact that is missing named, and is never guessed into one of the other four

rule.why_undecidable_is_second: a refusal is readable from the enclosing function whatever the glob resolves to, so REFUSES is decidable first. Every one of the three remaining classes needs the glob's member set resolved: CANNOT_SHRINK needs every matchable file shown tracked, and CAN_SHRINK_SILENTLY needs at least one shown untracked. If the member set does not resolve, NONE of the three is decidable, and placing UNDECIDABLE last would let the residual class CAN_SHRINK_SILENTLY collect every site whose directory simply could not be read -- which would inflate the finding this lane exists to measure. Placing it second makes an unresolved glob say so instead of accusing the site

variation_classes.LEGITIMATE_SCOPE: the result's OWN declared scope accounts for the count it declares: either the result's parameters state a member list or a count equal to the declared member count, or an exclusion in that same result names every missing member. A chr21-only result declaring 1 where a genome-wide one declares 24, with the narrower scope STATED IN THE ARTEFACT, is this class
variation_classes.SILENT_SHRINK: all four conditions of `globcensus.is_shrink_v2` hold, carried whole and not weakened: the declared count is below the result's OWN declared scope; the missing members are present in the store today; no exclusion in that result names them; AND the missing members CARRY DATA the result's own scope would have used. The fourth condition is lane-shrinkimpact's and is the one that refuted stage 2 -- without it a labelling artefact and an empty chromosome look exactly like a shrink from the manifest alone
variation_classes.UNDECIDABLE: the artefact does not state a scope the count can be read against, or it states one but the fourth condition cannot be settled without opening the members and recomputing, which this lane does not do. IF THE ARTEFACT DOES NOT STATE ITS SCOPE THE HONEST CLASS IS UNDECIDABLE AND NOT 'PROBABLY FINE'. This class is declared in advance as a legitimate outcome and is the expected one wherever a recomputation would be needed

prewritten_outcomes.all_18_cannot_shrink: the mechanism is INERT at every site: every glob reads a git-tracked directory, so the defect of 2026-10-11 has no live site in this repository and the existing tracked-file guards already cover it. The report would then say the mechanism is real in 18 places, realised in 0 of the 6 checked, and ineffective at all 18 by construction -- and the named fix would be documentation only
prewritten_outcomes.some_can_shrink_silently: those sites are named with path:line as the LIVE sites of the defect, with the untracked store each one globs. The report names a fix and does not perform it: the shape would be a refusal or an expected-member list recorded beside the group. No count of live sites is a count of realised shrinks -- lane-shrinkimpact found 0 of 6 realised -- and the report will not let the two be read as one number
prewritten_outcomes.most_undecidable: reported as the answer, with the missing fact named per site. ALL UNDECIDABLE FROM THE CODE IS A COMPLETE ANSWER and not a failure of the lane: it would establish that the defect cannot be triaged statically, which is itself the finding, and it would name what a decidable version of the question requires
prewritten_outcomes.the_six_varying: each gets one of LEGITIMATE_SCOPE, SILENT_SHRINK or UNDECIDABLE with the ARTEFACT FIELD that decided it quoted. UNDECIDABLE is expected for any group whose fourth condition needs a recomputation, and is reported as such rather than softened

inherited.limit_carried_verbatim: a group CONSTANT at a shrunken value is invisible to that method, so the 82 constant groups -- including the 13 that all say 312 -- are NOT shown safe
inherited.stage_2_refuted: REALISED IN 0 OF 6. closure_cell_inventory's chr21 WAS READ and was filed under another group's label -- a prefix-grouping artefact, not an absence; verified here independently, chr21 is present in that same result's all-enhancer sweep group (70 files) and its local element-table group (23), and missing only from GENCODE's. chrY is not in the CRISPRi library at all. why_a_second_pass: the first pass's FACTS were too loose in three named ways, and each tightening is the registered wording of VARIATION_CLASSES applied more strictly rather than a change to it. (1) COMMENSURABLE SCOPE: LEGITIMATE_SCOPE requires the result's own declared scope to ACCOUNT FOR the count it declares, and a 24-chromosome list does not account for a 73-FILE group -- the all-enhancer sweep passed the first pass only because 73 >= 24, a comparison of files against chromosomes that means nothing. Where the declared count EXCEEDS the stated scope the two are not commensurable and the artefact states no scope this count can be read against. (2) EXCLUSIONS: the rule requires an exclusion to name EVERY MISSING MEMBER, and a substring hit on 'chr' establishes nothing of the kind -- globcensus found closure_cell_inventory naming chrY and NOT chr21, which is exactly the case the loose test would flatter. Unless the missing members are known and each named, the fact is UNESTABLISHED, not false. (3) PRESENCE IN THE STORE: for the two groups lane-shrinkimpact recomputed, condition (2) was MEASURED true and is carried from its record rather than left unknown, which is what lets its settled fourth condition decide them
the_refinement_not_taken: condition (3) of the shrink test -- 'no exclusion in that result names them' -- is establishable NEGATIVELY: where no exclusion mentions any chromosome token at all, no exclusion can name the missing members, so the fact is FALSE and not unknown. Supplied that way, three declarations of per_element_response_cache (hct116_count, reptest_answerable, rescore_cost) would have all three conditions known, lane-shrinkimpact's settled fourth condition would decide them, and they would move from UNDECIDABLE to LEGITIMATE_SCOPE. THIS PASS DOES NOT DO IT, for one reason: it moves declarations AWAY from undecidability, which is the flattering direction, and this lane has already corrected its facts once in that same direction's favour. A third pass that keeps making the answer tidier is how a rule fixed in advance stops meaning anything. The verdict reported is the one the rule gives on the facts as established, and for those six declarations lane-shrinkimpact's recomputation -- realised in 0 of 6 -- is the stronger and independent answer to the IMPACT question, which is not the question this rule asks
which_pass_is_the_answer: the CORRECTED pass. The first is kept beside it because the error is instructive: its loose facts made the all-enhancer sweep read LEGITIMATE_SCOPE on 73 files against a 24-chromosome list, and made two results read LEGITIMATE_SCOPE on a substring hit for 'chr' in their exclusions. Both would have understated the undecidability
